changes.walking: Continuous light-stick travel uses retimed native gaits, matching incoming velocity classes, post-ranking gait preference and real native walking touches below the old idle deadband.
changes.heel: A small planned whole-player support arc avoids early ankle-ball collisions; both trajectory endpoints, native joint tracks and the authored contact time are preserved. No collider is disabled.
changes.support: Damped pelvis compression and tilt recruit both knees through two-bone IK; original shoe positions and orientations are retained, horizontal root travel stays native, next-contact preparation relaxes the load.
changes.falls: Muscle tone persists during free fall; bracing uses the actual trunk orientation; recovery hands back a valid native idle while preserving temporal pose buffers.
changes.keepers: Dive candidates reject the wrong incoming side at their own contact time; intentional backpasses are anticipated and intercepted with native foot actions.
changes.receptions: Forecasts include braking; CPU approaches and the real control impulse respect the planned outgoing movement.
changes.restarts: Bounded off-ball runs during free kicks, corners, throw-ins and goal kicks, without early ball contact.
changes.passing: Human A uses a monotonic 3.2 to 22.2 m/s short-pass curve from actual button charge.
changes.audio: Original synthesized turf steps, breathing and outdoor ambience; impact gain increased; step events follow actual foot plants.

procedural.generated_action_scope: Ankle, torso and shoulder variations of 10 native actions; source root, hips, knees, duration and contact markers unchanged.
procedural.support_scope: Runtime support response is separate from the baked actions and upper-body profile layer.

investigated_findings: Native velocity classes, motion ranking and touch-request deadbands initially rejected walking; all three were corrected, preserving full-stick speed.
Short 500 ms measurements aliased the 1.68 second retimed gait. Walking is measured over multiple complete strides, with independent ball-contact and progressive-speed assertions.
A heel kick initially hit the ball accidentally with the preparing ankle. The planner measures real skin clearance and adds the smallest viable bounded support arc.
